result.title: ScopeMem: Latent Memory That Learns Where to Revise Frozen GUI Agents
result.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Zhicheng Zheng and Cheng Zhang contributed equally
result.summary: Latent memory is gaining ground as a lightweight history supplement for GUI agents. It supplies history to a frozen vision-language model via prefix vectors trained with step-wise cross-entropy (CE). While resulting gains are naturally attributed to encoded history, our controlled experiments show they primarily stem from action revision. The prefix learns to alter the model's default actions. However, this revision is unscoped because step-wise CE pushes outputs toward reference actions at every step without explicitly preserving correct decisions. Consequently, it repairs errors but also breaks 8-13% of initially correct answers. Overall accuracy metrics hide these losses. We therefore propose ScopeMem, a latent-memory method for scoped revision. Its encoder conditions prefix generation on the model's initial answer and is trained to correct errors while preserving correct decisions. On the controlled ablation set, ScopeMem reduces the share of broken correct decisions to 5.6% while repairing more errors than any evaluated CE-trained prefix. On AndroidControl, GUI-Odyssey, and zero-shot AITW, ScopeMem outperforms all evaluated prompting and latent-memory baselines, enabling a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B to match or surpass GUI-specialized agents and Qwen3-VL-32B.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究给冻结 VLM 的 GUI 智能体提供 latent memory（prefix 向量）的做法：控制实验表明逐步 CE 训练出的前缀带来的提升主要来自「动作修正」而非历史编码，且会无差别地改坏 8–13% 原本正确的决策；为此提出 ScopeMem，以模型初始答案为条件生成前缀，只做有范围的修正，并在 AndroidControl、GUI-Odyssey、AITW 等基准上超过提示与 latent-memory 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接触及 latent 前缀作为推理期状态的使用方式与训练监督目标，指出准确率指标会掩盖「原本正确决策被改坏」，与 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真被使用、收益贡献分配及保留正确信息的问题高度相关，可供核查其控制实验与「有范围修正」的判定设计。
